name: Rootglow — Bioluminescent Heritage Pattern Culture
creator: Geneware collective Iyawo Synthesis Lab; popularized through Fluxskin annual convergence
description: A geneware expression movement in which practitioners use bioluminescent dermal modification to render patterns drawn from their family heritage — kente geometry, ikat repetition, Celtic knotwork, rangoli symmetry, moko line, whakapapa genealogical mapping — as living light beneath the skin. Unlike static tattoo culture, Rootglow patterns respond to emotion, temperature, and BCI state, brightening under stress, shifting hue with mood, fading during sleep. The movement explicitly frames this as an answer to the Ubiquitous Diaspora question of heritage: when everything is mixed, what do you carry? You carry what you choose, and you make it glow.
medium: geneware body modification; Fluxskin circuit events; neural feed documentation; physical photography archive
cultural_impact: Rootglow became the dominant geneware fashion movement of the 2210s and forced a serious cultural conversation about what heritage means when ancestry is algorithmically reconstructed from genetic data rather than lived tradition. Critics argued that wearing patterns from traditions one has no cultural connection to beyond a DNA percentage is a form of decorative extraction; practitioners argued that in a fully interbred world, any other framing is artificial scarcity.
controversy: The heritage authenticity debate within Rootglow is ongoing and sometimes vicious. Several geneware artists have published 'pattern ethics' frameworks arguing for community consultation before adopting specific traditional geometries; others reject this as imposing pre-Diaspora identity categories on a post-Diaspora world. At least one high-profile Fluxskin exhibition was physically disrupted by protesters objecting to specific pattern appropriations.
story_hooks: A character's Rootglow pattern — chosen from reconstructed ancestral data — begins displaying a geometric sequence that no known heritage tradition uses, and a geneware artist recognizes it as something else entirely.

A Tier 5 fashion house has begun licensing 'heritage pattern libraries' for Rootglow applications, paying communities for aesthetic rights — and someone is discovering that the licensing agreements contain clauses that transfer something far more valuable.
Two people meet at a Fluxskin event wearing identical patterns from different heritage traditions that have no known historical connection, and neither of them can explain why.
